answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence reputation or receive work. A verifier randomly selects tasks, checks submitted evidence, and slashes the stake when an identity is caught duplicating another agent’s claims; honest agents recover theirs over time. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock capital in every persona and risks losing it, rather than multiplying influence for free. A falcon, jade, or lantern can name a test task, but none bypasses the same stake and audit.
